body.statement:
There is a finite constant \(K_{\mathrm{res}}\), depending only on
\((c,C,G)\), such that for every \(N\geq N_0\),
\[
 \sup_{p\in\mathcal P,\,|\gamma|\leq G}
 \mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}
 \left|\{G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N}\}
 h_{1,N}(X_{1,N})\right|
 \leq K_{\mathrm{res}}N^{-1/2}.
\]
This bound includes every state for which an available upward or downward
lattice jump crosses \(\gamma_N\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\delta=N^{-1/2}\) and \(g=\gamma_N\).  Since \(|g-\gamma|\leq\delta\), it suffices to work on the enlarged compact staffing window \([-G-1,G+1]\).  The derivative bound in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) gives \(1/D\leq h_g'\leq1/d\).  Its Poisson equation is
\[
 qh_g''(x)=-(x-m_g)-b_g(x)h_g'(x),
 \qquad b_g(x)=-dx-\nu\min(x,g).                                \tag{30}
\]
Applying the stationary diffusion identity to \(x^2\), and using \(x\min(x,g)\geq-(G+1)|x|\), gives a compact-uniform second-moment bound and hence a uniform bound on \(|m_g|\).  Equation (30) then implies
\[
 |h_g''(x)|\leq C_1(1+|x|).                                     \tag{31}
\]
On either open side of \(g\), differentiation gives
\[
 qh_g'''(x)=-1-b_g'(x)h_g'(x)-b_g(x)h_g''(x),                   \tag{32}
\]
where \(b_g'=-D\) to the left and \(b_g'=-d\) to the right.  Thus
\[
 |h_g'''(x)|\leq C_2(1+x^2)                                    \tag{33}
\]
away from the kink.  The drift, \(h_g'\), and the right side of (30) are continuous at \(g\), so \(h_g''\) is continuous there.  Hence \(h_g''\) is locally absolutely continuous and Taylor's formula with integral remainder is valid even when the jump interval meets or crosses the kink.

At the lattice state \(x=(k-Na)/\sqrt N\), let \(B_N(x)\) and \(D_N(x)\) be the available upward and downward rates.  Direct algebra gives, including at the endpoints where the unavailable rate is zero,
\[
 \delta(B_N-D_N)=b_g(x),
 \qquad
 \frac{\delta^2}{2}(B_N+D_N)
 =q+\frac\delta2\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}.                \tag{34}
\]
Taylor expansion with (31)--(33) therefore yields
\[
\begin{split}
 G_{1,N}h_g(x)
 &=b_g(x)h_g'(x)
 +\left[q+\frac\delta2\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}\right]h_g''(x)
 +R_N(x),\\
 |R_N(x)|
 &\leq\frac{\delta^3}{6}\{B_N(x)+D_N(x)\}
       \sup_{|u-x|\leq\delta}|h_g'''(u)|
 \leq C_3\delta(1+x^2).                                        \tag{35}
\end{split}
\]
Here \(B_N+D_N\leq3CN\).  The additional second-derivative term in (35) is bounded by \(C_4\delta(1+x^2)\) using (31).  Subtracting \(\mathcal L_gh_g=b_gh_g'+qh_g''\) gives the pointwise bound
\[
 |(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_g)h_g(x)|\leq C_5\delta(1+x^2).           \tag{36}
\]

An independent stationary drift calculation from (34) gives
\[
 G_{1,N}x^2
 =2xb_g(x)+2q+\delta\{(\tau-\lambda)x+\nu\min(x,g)\}
 \leq-dx^2+C_6.                                                  \tag{37}
\]
Stationarity implies \(\sup_{N,p,\gamma}\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}X_{1,N}^2\leq C_6/d\).  Taking expectations in (36) proves the displayed theorem with \(K_{\mathrm{res}}=C_5(1+C_6/d)\).

This is also an analytic early-kill check.  The proof is pointwise at every lattice state, includes the two physical endpoints, and treats the kink edge by absolute continuity; the exact product law only enters through stationary expectation.  Hence every ceiling phase and every asymmetric corner of \([c,C]^3\) is controlled by the same finite constant.  In the smallest interior chain \(N=2,M_N=1\), the three states are precisely the left endpoint, kink, and right endpoint, so (34)--(36) enumerate every available jump and leave no untested transition.  Finally, stationarity and the Poisson equation give
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}X_{1,N}-m_{\gamma_N}\right|
 =\left|\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}}
   [(G_{1,N}-\mathcal L_{\gamma_N})h_{1,N}(X_{1,N})]\right|
 \leq K_{\mathrm{res}}N^{-1/2}.                                \tag{38}
\]
Thus the scaled residual cannot have a nonvanishing order-one component at a corner or ceiling phase.
body.justification: The pointwise Taylor envelope and stationary moment bound prove the previously isolated residual uniformly through the moving kink.
body.gap: This theorem now closes, rather than merely states, the finite-to-diffusion centering remainder.
body.consumer: It certifies when the simpler diffusion fitted center can replace exact product-law evaluation.
